groups.notes: No numeric late-adaptation pointing error is printed for old subjects on these pages. The per-episode means and SDs exist only in Fig. 1 as a chart ('Mean pointing errors of young (triangles) and old (squares) subjects before, during, and after exposure to rotated visual feedback... Also shown are the standard deviations'), which may not be read off. The only numbers relating to the end of adaptation are parameters of a fitted equation: 'An exponential fit yielded y=9.92+53.51\u00d7exp(\u2212x/5.89) for young subjects and y=29.51+29.91\u00d7exp(\u2212x/5.13) for old subjects.' (asymptote 29.51 for old) — a fit parameter, not a reported episode value, so not transcribed. Page 4 also reports 'The magnitude of adaptation in this sample was 0.49\u00b10.21', but that is a unitless adaptation-magnitude index for a pooled sample of 54 seniors ('our sample size thus increased to 54 seniors aged 64.0\u00b14.5 years'), not the 12 old experimental subjects, and not the late-adaptation angular error. Statistical results only: 'significant effects were yielded for Age (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05), Episode (F(14,308)=41.14, P<0.001), and their interaction (F(14,308)=3.44, P<0.001).'

No numeric late-adaptation pointing error is printed for young subjects on these pages. Fig. 1 shows the episode-by-episode means and SDs graphically only. The only end-of-adaptation-related number is the asymptote of a fitted curve: 'An exponential fit yielded y=9.92+53.51\u00d7exp(\u2212x/5.89) for young subjects and y=29.51+29.91\u00d7exp(\u2212x/5.13) for old subjects.' (asymptote 9.92 for young) — a fit parameter rather than a reported episode value, so not transcribed. Trail-making values (27.4\u00b17.2 s young; 42.5\u00b16.9 s old) are a different outcome.

parsed.notes: Pages 3–4 contain no tables; the adaptation time course is presented only in Fig. 1 (pointing errors) and Fig. 2 (tracking errors) as figures, with no printed per-episode values. Nothing on these pages states a block-average or final-episode pointing error in degrees for either age group. Candidate numbers considered and rejected: (1) exponential-fit asymptotes 9.92 deg (young) and 29.51 deg (old) — parameters of a fitted equation, not a reported measured value, and no dispersion given; (2) adaptation magnitude A = 0.49\u00b10.21, which applies to a pooled sample of 54 seniors from supplementary unpublished experiments, with no corresponding young value printed.
